hypotheses.name: specification insufficiency
hypotheses.claim: the prompt does not contain enough information to deduce the correct expected value
supporting_signature: base and SFT both low on P(correct oracle | disc)
Probe A: only A4 (behavioural evidence) raises the conditional oracle rate; A1-A3 do not
weakening_signature: Probe A: A1/A2/A3 raise the conditional oracle rate by >= 5 points

hypotheses.name: objective mismatch
hypotheses.claim: next-token imitation of whole tests does not optimise oracle correctness; it shifts input choice more than value prediction
hypotheses.mediator: P(disc | execute) up and P(correct oracle | disc) flat or down under SFT
supporting_signature: Phase 2: SFT raises P(disc|execute) while P(correct oracle|disc) falls
Phase 4: oracle-only or verifier-filtered supervision raises P(correct oracle|disc) >= 5 points where arm-A-style SFT does not
weakening_signature: Phase 2: SFT raises P(correct oracle | disc)
hypotheses.decisive_test: Phase 2, then a Phase 4 single-factor arm

hypotheses.name: adapter/model capacity
hypotheses.claim: a 1.5B model with the current LoRA cannot acquire execution semantics
hypotheses.mediator: output-prediction accuracy on fixed discriminating inputs
supporting_signature: Probe C: a larger or full-capacity model raises constrained output-prediction accuracy while the 1.5B adapters do not
weakening_signature: Probe C: a larger model does not beat 1.5B base on constrained output prediction

hypotheses.name: dataset-distribution shift
hypotheses.claim: synthetic supervision does not represent the evaluated behaviour; gains stay on the training distribution
hypotheses.mediator: train-vs-held-out gap in P(correct oracle | disc) for the same checkpoint
supporting_signature: SFT raises P(correct oracle|disc) on training functions but not on held-out functions
weakening_signature: SFT does not raise P(correct oracle|disc) even on its own training functions

hypotheses.name: contract degradation
hypotheses.claim: SFT damages output form (parse, policy, execution, verbosity, non-answers) and that causes the validity loss
hypotheses.mediator: P(parse), P(execute|parse), policy-invalid rate, assertion count
supporting_signature: Phase 2: the validity loss sits in parse/execute/contract stages
Probe B: constrained output recovers validity and Kill@8
weakening_signature: Phase 2: parse and execution are unchanged or better and the validity loss sits at the oracle stage

hypotheses.name: overfitting / forgetting
hypotheses.claim: training fits development-specific patterns and loses broadly useful base behaviour as steps increase
hypotheses.mediator: P(correct oracle | disc) and diversity along the training trajectory
supporting_signature: Phase 2 trajectory: the conditional oracle rate declines with steps while training loss falls
the decline is steepest where diversity collapses (duplicates rise)
weakening_signature: the conditional oracle rate is flat or rising across steps

hypotheses.name: insufficient evaluation power
hypotheses.claim: +3.43 points may be real but unresolvable at the available cluster count
hypotheses.mediator: cluster-bootstrap interval width of the Kill@8 difference
supporting_signature: the clustered 95% interval of the Kill@8 difference includes both 0 and +3 points
weakening_signature: the clustered interval excludes +3 points (either side)
hypotheses.decisive_test: Phase 2 clustered inference plus a minimum-detectable-effect calculation
